transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-25 16:30 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Jessica Liu (CobaltPayments Eng), Tom Reynolds (CobaltPayments SRE), Ravi Khatri (CobaltPayments PM)

Summary: quick steady-state throughput review after last week's tuning (kv cache priming, continuous batching changes, and queue shaping). Goal: agree final concurrency targets for canary and handoff to CSM/ops.

Topics covered: throughput numbers, per-token cost tradeoffs, backpressure behavior, burst capacity, security/SSO/retention check, handoff checklist.

[00:00] Aisha: ok everyone thanks for joining, I think we've got 45 minutes on the clock, main things today are the steady state numbers and the handoff plan. Marco will walk us through the numbers first.
[00:22] Marco: cool, yeah I pulled the last 72 hour run, so remember we enabled continuous batching on Tuesday and increased the batch window from 8ms to 18ms, that netted about 14% token cost reduction and a 6 to 12 ms median latency change depending on seq len. there is some variance at the tails.
[00:45] Jessica: right so locally we saw the median go up a bit for single-request latency, but p99 improved yes, p99 is better with batching because it amortizes overhead. we care about 95th and 99th for user flows.
[01:10] Tom: can you clarify the exact concurrency numbers you used for those runs? last week we were at 32 concurrent workers per instance.
[01:25] Marco: for the steady-state we ran at 32, 48 and 64 ceilings. 32 had best single-request median but lower throughput. at 48 we hit 1.9x throughput vs 32 with 10ms higher median. at 64 we saw diminishing returns and a little more queueing at the front end.
[01:50] Aisha: key customer ask is to pick a safe canary value so the ops team can run the configuration.
[02:00] Ravi: our SLA target is 300ms median and <500ms p95 for the payment auth flow, which is a bit tighter than some other flows. Are those numbers compatible?
[02:18] Marco: yes for the prompt lengths you shared (avg 220 tokens) median hovered ~180-200ms at 48 concurrency with continuous batching engaged, p95 was around 420ms. so fits in the window but p99 can spike in heavy long tails if KV cache misses occur during burst.
[02:45] Jessica: about KV cache — we noticed some cold-starts where the KV cache priming didn't fully warm across all shards, the transcript from the last run shows some 900ms outliers, likely our request fan-out pattern.
[03:05] Marco: correct, and part of that is the current routing which sends some requests to lower utilization hosts; we suggested enabling prefix caching for those specific frequent routes. also our suggest is to use a short pre-warm ramp before peak traffic windows.
[03:30] Tom: what about fallback plans? if we hit capacity, do we have automatic downgrade to a smaller model or region fallback?
[03:42] Aisha: yes, Redwood platform can fallback by policy to a compatible model variant with lower cost/latency or route to dedicated pool if reserved capacity is available — you can set a policy that prefers latency or cost. for the POC you wanted predictable latency so we recommended a dedicated-capacity reserve for peak windows but keep hosted for normal.
[04:05] Ravi: that reserved capacity is interesting but procurement needs to know the cost delta. we need to see the unit economics after batching is fully enabled.
[04:20] Marco: on cost: the 14% token cost reduction I mentioned translates to approx 9% lower per-auth cost once you factor concurrency and amortization. i can put a worked example in the spreadsheet.
[04:35] Jessica: do we have a clear number on queue_size and queueing policy? in one run we saw queue depth grow to 220 requests and then the front-end started shedding.
[04:50] Marco: in that test the front-end queue_size was 256; however shedding configured at 200. our recommended steady-state is to set queue_size to 320 with soft backpressure at 240 and hard at 320 so you get smoother shaping.
[05:15] Aisha: whether to push that higher depends on how tolerant the downstream is to increased latency. if you prioritize median latency keep smaller queue, if you prioritize throughput raise it.
[05:30] Tom: security/regulatory note — procurement needs SOC 2 docs and SSO/SAML integration for the private config before we can sign for reserved capacity.
[05:45] Aisha: understood, i'll attach the compliance pack; we already have SOC 2 Type II and can walk you through the SSO setup with the private control plane, and there's KMS/HSM options for key management.
[06:00] Ravi: also need audit logs retention settings for 12 months and the ability to disable retention for PII routes.
[06:12] Marco: yes, audit logs can be routed to your log collector or to the private lane, retention and masking controls are configurable per-route.
[06:25] Jessica: back to throughput, can we talk about continuous batching knobs? you mentioned batch window tuning — how sensitive is the system to that?
[06:40] Marco: pretty sensitive for short prompts. increasing from 8ms to 18ms boosted batching across the 200 token average, but for very short 20–40 token prompts it's marginal and hurts median. recommended approach: use adaptive batching that adjusts window based on observed inter-arrival time per route. we have a config to set min/max window and target batch size.
[07:05] Aisha: ok so recommendation for canary: concurrency ceiling of 48, queue soft=240 hard=320, adaptive batching with window min=6ms max=22ms, and prefix cache enabled for top 20 routes.
[07:25] Tom: sounds reasonable, but can we try two burst tests: one 10 minute peak at expected max qps and one 30 minute gradual ramp to see tail behavior?
[07:40] Marco: yes we can run both. proposed windows: peak burst at 1.8x expected peak for 10 min, and a ramp from 0.5x to 2x over 30 minutes. we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and cpu/gpu utilization.
[07:55] Jessica: who owns running those tests?
[08:00] Aisha: Redwood will run the tests with your ops in the loop; Marco will execute the runbook, Jessica will provide test harness access and Tom will monitor infra.
[08:12] Ravi: timeline? we'd like this before we move to canary at the start of next week.
[08:20] Marco: we can do a first burst on Friday 2026-11-27 if you can reserve an ops window. second longer ramp Monday morning, 2026-11-30.
[08:35] Jessica: Friday works but need to confirm with site reliability team, i'll add it to my calendar and send invites.
[08:45] Aisha: perfect. for handoff, after successful runs we want to bring CSM in and create a runbook snapshot in the customers workspace. then the CSM will own canary monitoring and SLA alerts.
[09:00] Tom: quick question about instrumentation: what telemetry will we get out of box?
[09:08] Marco: you'll get token-level cost, per-request latency histograms, batch sizes, KV cache hit rates, GPU utilization and per-route tracing hooks. we can add custom tags to link to your payment flow.
[09:25] Aisha: any blockers on your side for the burst tests?
[09:30] Jessica: only getting final approval for the ops window and a short whitelist for test traffic IPs.
[09:36] Ravi: procurement still needs the compliance pack before reserved capacity procurement, but that can be parallel.
[09:45] Aisha: we'll send the compliance docs and benchmark sheet after this call. i'll also share the recommended config and the canary plan.
[09:55] Marco: one more note — we noticed one host that showed GC-like pauses in logs during the 64 concurrency run; it's probably runtime memory pressure on that VM. recommend increasing pre-warm and slightly lowering per-host concurrency if you can't expand instance size.
[10:20] Tom: good catch, we'll look at instance sizing. that may affect procurement decision.
[10:30] Jessica: ok to recap?
[10:35] Aisha: recap — agree to canary default: concurrency 48, queue soft 240/hard 320, adaptive batching min 6ms max 22ms, prefix cache top 20 routes, run two burst tests (11/27 and 11/30), Marco to post config and spreadsheet, Aisha to send compliance pack and schedule CSM handoff next week.
[10:55] Ravi: yes agreed.
[11:00] Aisha: action items we'll put in the notes — Marco you'll post runtime config, i'll send benchmark sheet and compliance, Jessica to confirm ops windows.
[11:12] Marco: i'll capture the config and put the runbook link in the slack channel.
[11:20] Jessica: will do calendar invites by EOD.
[11:30] Aisha: thanks all, speak soon.
